definition_zh: 生产率；生产力；产出效率
definition_en: the rate at which work produces output, measured as output per unit of labour, land or capital
core_image: 一台机器前站着一名工人，出口处的成品箱一层层堆高，时钟却只走了一小格
scene: 这里指「生产率」。 Productivity rose after the old machines were replaced.
sceneCN: 这里 productivity 是「生产率」（第 1 个义项：单位投入的产出效率）；句意：旧机器更换之后生产率上升了。图中可辨识物件：机器、工人、堆高的成品箱、只走了一小格的时钟。

pos.zh: 生产率；生产力；产出效率

senses.title: Output per input
senses.titleCN: 生产率：一份投入换多少产出
senses.definition: the ratio of output produced to the input used, such as hours worked or land farmed
senses.definitionCN: 产出与所用投入（如工时或耕地）之比
senses.example: Productivity doubled after the assembly line was redesigned.
senses.exampleCN: 装配线重新设计后，生产率翻了一番。
senses.why: producere means 'to lead forth'. Productivity measures how much is led forth from a given effort, which makes it a ratio.
senses.whyCN: producere 意为“向前引出”。生产率衡量一份投入能引出多少产出，所以它是一个比率。

senses.title: Labour productivity
senses.titleCN: 劳动生产率：每人每小时产出
senses.definition: output per hour or per worker, the most common economic measure
senses.definitionCN: 每工时或每人产出，最常见的经济指标
senses.example: Labour productivity in manufacturing grew by three percent.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业劳动生产率增长百分之三。
senses.why: Hours are the denominator economists use most, because labour is the input that can be counted most cleanly.
senses.whyCN: 工时是经济学家最常用的分母，因为劳动是最容易清楚计数的投入。

senses.title: Agricultural productivity
senses.titleCN: 农业生产力：一亩地打多少粮
senses.definition: output per hectare or per farm worker in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中每公顷或每个农业劳动者的产出
senses.example: Higher agricultural productivity freed workers for cities.
senses.exampleCN: 农业生产力提高，使劳动者得以流向城市。
senses.why: Land was the original denominator. When yields rise, the same field feeds more people, and that is productivity.
senses.whyCN: 土地是最初的分母。产量提高时，同一块田能养活更多人，这就是生产力。

senses.title: Productivity growth
senses.titleCN: 生产率增长：效率在变好
senses.definition: the rate at which the output-to-input ratio improves over time
senses.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比随时间改善的速度
senses.example: Productivity growth stalled for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 生产率增长停滞了十年。
senses.why: Growth turns a level into a trend. Economists care about the direction because small yearly gains compound.
senses.whyCN: 增长把水平变成趋势。经济学家关心方向，因为每年小幅提升会复利累积。

senses.title: Office productivity
senses.titleCN: 办公效率：工具让你更快
senses.definition: in computing and marketing, the capacity of a person or tool to complete work, as in productivity software
senses.definitionCN: 在计算与营销语境中指人或工具完成工作的能力，如办公效率软件
senses.example: The suite is sold as productivity software.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件以办公效率软件的名义出售。
senses.why: Software marketing borrowed the economic word and dropped the denominator, so it now means roughly 'gets work done'.
senses.whyCN: 软件营销借用了经济词却去掉了分母，于是现在大致意为“能把活干完”。

senses.title: Total factor productivity
senses.titleCN: 全要素生产率：剩下那部分增长
senses.definition: the part of output growth not explained by more labour or capital, often taken as technical progress
senses.definitionCN: 产出增长中无法由劳动或资本增加解释的部分，常被视为技术进步
senses.example: Total factor productivity explains most long-run growth.
senses.exampleCN: 全要素生产率解释了大部分长期增长。
senses.why: Economics needs a residual for what it cannot measure. The term names that leftover, which is why it is also called the residual.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要一个“测不出来的剩余”。这个词命名那块剩余，所以它又叫残差。

senses.title: Ecological productivity
senses.titleCN: 生态生产力：生态系统造出多少有机物
senses.definition: in ecology, the rate at which an ecosystem produces biomass, as in primary productivity
senses.definitionCN: 生态学上指生态系统生产生物量的速率，如初级生产力
senses.example: Primary productivity in the lake fell after the bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 水华之后湖水的初级生产力下降。
senses.why: Ecology transfers the ratio from factories to living systems: sunlight and nutrients are the input, biomass is the output.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把比率从工厂搬到生命系统：阳光与养分是投入，生物量是产出。

senses.title: The productivity paradox
senses.titleCN: 生产率悖论：投了电脑却不见增长
senses.definition: the observed mismatch between heavy investment in technology and weak measured productivity growth
senses.definitionCN: 大量技术投入与测得的疲弱生产率增长之间的落差
senses.example: The productivity paradox delayed the promised office revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 生产率悖论推迟了人们许诺的办公革命。
senses.why: Measurement lag explains part of the paradox: gains appear only after work is reorganised around the new tools.
senses.whyCN: 测量滞后解释了部分悖论：只有围绕新工具重组工作后，收益才显现。

intro.en: Productivity comes from Latin producere 'to lead forth, bring out', from pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead'. The abstract noun is productivitas, formed in later Latin.
intro.cn: productivity 来自拉丁 producere“向前引出、产生”，由 pro-“向前”加 ducere“引导”构成，抽象名词 productivitas 为晚期拉丁构成。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead'. It underlies conduct, reduce, introduce and educate, each with its own prefix direction.
items.cn: ducere 意为“引导”。它支撑 conduct、reduce、introduce、educate，各接不同方向的前缀。

items.en: pro- 'forward' plus ducere gives producere, 'to lead or bring forth'. The image is leading something out into view.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 ducere 构成 producere“引出、产生”。意象是把东西引出来让人看见。

items.en: The participle productum 'brought forth' gives English product: the thing led out. Production names the leading-out act.
items.cn: 分词 productum“被引出之物”给出英语 product。production 命名“引出”这个动作。

items.en: Later Latin forms productivitas on the adjective productivus, meaning 'having the power to produce'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语以形容词 productivus“有产出能力的”构成 productivitas。

items.en: English adopts productivity in the age of agricultural improvement, first as the quality of being productive.
items.cn: 英语在农业改良时代采用 productivity，最初指“多产的性质”。

items.en: In the 20th century economics fixes the quantitative sense: output divided by input, tracked as a growth series.
items.cn: 20 世纪经济学固定了数量义：产出除以投入，作为增长序列来追踪。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duc- stem or the -ivity ending; the near-meaning group all concern output, differing in unit and scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duc- 词干或 -ivity 结尾；近义组都关乎产出，差别在单位与尺度。

entries.definition: yielding results or output. The adjective describes the worker or land; productivity measures the ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 多产的；有成效的。形容词描述工人或土地，productivity 度量比率。

entries.definition: the total amount produced. It is a quantity, while productivity is that quantity per unit of input.
entries.definitionCN: 产量。它是总量，而 productivity 是每单位投入的产量。

entries.definition: the item produced. It is the noun for what comes out, not for how efficiently it came out.
entries.definitionCN: 产品。它命名产出物，而非产出效率。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful work to the energy or resources spent. It stresses waste avoided, while productivity stresses output per input.
entries.definitionCN: 效率。它强调避免了浪费，而 productivity 强调单位投入的产出。

entries.definition: the amount produced in a period. It is what productivity divides by input.
entries.definitionCN: 产出量。它是 productivity 用来除以投入的那个分子。

entries.definition: the amount harvested from land. It is a physical output, close to productivity when measured per hectare.
entries.definitionCN: 产量。它是土地的实物产出，按公顷衡量时接近 productivity。

entries.definition: the volume passing through a system in a time. It counts flow, not output per unit of effort.
entries.definitionCN: 吞吐量。它统计流量，而非单位投入的产出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead' gives 'lead forth', which is the source of produce, product and productivity.
normal.cn: pro-“向前”加 ducere“引导”得“引出”，是 produce、product、productivity 的共同来源。

normal.en: The word is a fraction: output on top, input on the bottom. Every collocation names one of the two halves.
normal.cn: 这个词是一个分数：产出在上，投入在下。每个搭配都在给其中一半命名。

normal.en: Labour productivity puts hours on the bottom; agricultural productivity puts hectares on the bottom.
normal.cn: 劳动生产率把工时放在分母；农业生产力把公顷放在分母。

normal.en: Production is the total; productivity is the total divided by the effort.
normal.cn: production 是总量；productivity 是总量除以投入。

normal.en: The productivity paradox is the puzzle of paying for computers and not seeing the gain in the numbers.
normal.cn: 生产率悖论就是：花了钱买电脑，数字里却看不到收益。

abstract.en: Picture the same basket of apples carried out by fewer hands.
abstract.cn: 想象同样一篮苹果由更少的人手搬出来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that finishes the shift while the pile of boxes is twice as high.
abstract.cn: 想象一个班次结束时，箱子堆得比原来高一倍。

abstract.en: Picture a field that feeds two families where it once fed one.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田从养活一户人家变成养活两户。

examples.en: Productivity in the port improved when the cranes were automated.
examples.cn: 港口起重机自动化后，生产率提高了。

examples.en: Wage growth has lagged behind productivity growth.
examples.cn: 工资增长落后于生产率增长。

examples.en: Primary productivity is highest in shallow coastal water.
examples.cn: 初级生产力在浅海沿岸水域最高。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若达克提维梯”音近 productivity：先把东西“达”出来、再“克”住工时、效率就“提”上去 → productivity 生产率

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ ducere“引导”→ producere“引出、产生”；productivus + -itas 构成抽象名词 productivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much comes out for what goes in, and the differences come from which input is counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都衡量“进去多少、出来多少”，差别在数的是哪一种投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: more boxes out of the same hours.
core.cn: 核心意象：同样的工时，搬出更多箱子。

branches.en: THE RATIO: the general fraction and the labour version differ only in the denominator.
branches.cn: 比率：一般分数与劳动版本只差分母。

branches.en: LAND: agriculture counts hectares, the oldest input measure.
branches.cn: 土地：农业按公顷计数，是最古老的投入度量。

branches.en: TRENDS AND PUZZLES: growth tracks the ratio over time, and the paradox notes when it fails to move.
branches.cn: 趋势与悖论：增长追踪比率随时间的变化，悖论指出它不动的时候。

branches.en: MARKETING: software drops the denominator and keeps only 'gets work done'.
branches.cn: 营销：软件抽掉了分母，只留下“能把活干完”。

branches.en: RESIDUAL AND BIOMASS: economics and ecology both measure what the obvious inputs cannot explain.
branches.cn: 剩余与生物量：经济学与生态学都度量“明显投入解释不了的部分”。

intro.en: Productivity is productiv- plus -ity. The stem carries 'leading forth', and the suffix turns an adjective of capacity into an abstract measure.
intro.cn: productivity 是 productiv- 加 -ity。词干携带“引出”，后缀把表能力的形容词变成抽象度量。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'lead' → producere 'bring forth' → productivus 'producing'. The English family runs produce, product, production, productive, productivity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”→ producere“引出”→ productivus“有产出能力的”。英语词族为 produce、product、production、productive、productivity。

items.meaning: the act or total of making

items.exampleCN: 这是一次有成效的会议。

items.meaning: in a way that yields results
items.exampleCN: 他们一上午都干得很有成效。

definition_zh: 效率；高效；效率比
definition_en: the quality of doing something well without waste, or the ratio of useful output to the energy or effort put in
core_image: 同样一桶油，跑得更远的那辆车
scene: 工厂换掉漏气的管道后，每吨产品的耗电降了一半。 Engineers measured the gain in efficiency at every stage.
sceneCN: 这里 efficiency 是「效率」（第 1 个义项：有用产出与投入之比）；句意是工程师在每个环节测量效率的提升。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ency 得到，义为「高效的」
由 efficient 加 -ly 构成，义为「高效地」
由 efficient 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效；效率低下」

senses.title: Output compared with input
senses.definition: the ratio of useful work or output to the energy, time or effort supplied
senses.definitionCN: 有用功或产出与所投入的能量、时间或努力之比
senses.example: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。
senses.why: Efficientia named the power of a cause to produce an effect; measured, that power becomes a ratio of output to input.
senses.whyCN: efficientia 指原因产生效果的力量；一旦被测量，这份力量就成为产出与投入之比。

senses.title: Working well without waste
senses.definition: the quality of doing something well with little waste of time, money or energy
senses.definitionCN: 把事情做好而很少浪费时间、金钱或精力的品质
senses.example: The office is known for its efficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个办公室以高效著称。
senses.why: A thing that produces its effect without waste is efficient, and the quality it shows is efficiency.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却能产生效果的东西是 efficient，而它显露出的这种品质就是 efficiency。

senses.title: A measured instance of such a ratio
senses.definition: a particular measurement or instance of efficient performance, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某一具体的效率测量结果或表现，常用复数
senses.example: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。
senses.why: Once the ratio is counted, each count becomes a noun of its own, so the plural names separate figures.
senses.whyCN: 比值一旦被计数，每个计数就各自成为一个名词，于是复数指一项项分开的数字。

intro.en: Efficiency comes from Latin efficientia, the noun of efficere, through French efficience.
intro.cn: efficiency 来自拉丁语 efficientia（efficere 的名词），经法语 efficience 进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make, the base of the whole group.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是整个词组的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to accomplish or bring about.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「完成、做出」。

items.en: Efficientia named the power or action of producing a result.
items.cn: efficientia 指产生结果的力量或作用。

items.en: French passed the noun on with the sense of power to produce an effect.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词传下来，保留「产生效果的力量」之义。

items.en: Engineering and economics turned the abstract power into a measured ratio.
items.cn: 工程学与经济学把这种抽象力量变成可测量的比值。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficient family; the near-meaning group separates productivity, economy and effectiveness.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficient 词族；近义组区分 productivity、economy 与 effectiveness。

entries.definition: Working well without waste of time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高效的」，是本词的形容词词基。

entries.definition: In an efficient manner, without waste.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地、不浪费地」。

entries.definition: The quality of producing the wanted result, whether or not means are spared.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果是否达到，不管省不省。

entries.definition: Output per worker or per hour; efficiency measured in production.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生产率」，以产量衡量的效率。

entries.definition: Careful use of money and resources; the act of sparing rather than the ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节约」，指省用的行为，而不是比值。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, without any claim about cost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只讲能否达到预期结果，不谈成本。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one tank of fuel and ask how far it carries the car, then widen to offices and whole plants.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一桶油能跑多远出发，再扩到办公室与整座工厂。

normal.en: Efficiency asks: how much useful work comes out of what you put in?
normal.cn: efficiency 问的是：投进去的东西产出了多少有用的功？

normal.en: The same tank of fuel, a longer drive: that is fuel efficiency.
normal.cn: 同一桶油跑得更远，这就是 fuel efficiency。

normal.en: An office with efficiency gets the work done and leaves the lights off.
normal.cn: 高效的办公室把活干完，还顺手把灯关掉。

normal.en: Efficiency is the ratio; efficiencies are the separate figures you compare.
normal.cn: efficiency 是比值；efficiencies 是你拿来比较的一项项数字。

normal.en: Efficient is the adjective, efficiency the quality it shows.
normal.cn: efficient 是形容词，efficiency 是它显露出的品质。

abstract.en: Picture one barrel of oil and two cars leaving the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一桶油和两辆从同一条线出发的车。

abstract.en: The farther car turns the same barrel into more distance.
abstract.cn: 跑得更远的那辆车把同一桶油变成了更多里程。

abstract.en: Efficiency is that comparison written as a number.
abstract.cn: efficiency 就是把这种比较写成一个数字。

examples.en: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
examples.cn: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。

examples.en: The office is known for its efficiency.
examples.cn: 这个办公室以高效著称。

examples.en: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
examples.cn: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊菲申西」——漏气管道一换，同样的电做出更多产品

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其名词 efficientia 指「产生效果的力量」，经法语 efficience 进入英语，后转为可测量的产出投入之比。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficiency: the ratio of output to input, the quality of working without waste, and a measured instance of that ratio.
sensesIntro.cn: efficiency 的三个义项：产出与投入之比、不浪费地做好事情的品质，以及一项具体的效率测量值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one barrel of fuel carried farther by the better car.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶油，被更好的那辆车跑得更远。

branches.en: THE RATIO: useful output divided by what was put in.
branches.cn: 比值线：有用产出除以投入。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the work is done well and little is thrown away.
branches.cn: 习惯线：活干得好，扔掉的少。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: each measurement stands as its own count.
branches.cn: 数字线：每一次测量各自成为一项数字。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: a ratio only means something when figures are set side by side.
branches.cn: 比较线：比值只有把数字并排放在一起才有意义。

branches.en: THE SAVING: less waste is exactly what lifts the ratio.
branches.cn: 节约线：少浪费正是把比值抬上去的东西。

intro.en: Efficiency is a Latin-derived noun in -ency; English builds the adjective efficient and its adverb on the same stem.
intro.cn: efficiency 是以 -ency 收尾的拉丁语来源名词；英语在同一词干上构成形容词 efficient 及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficere and efficientia are recorded, so only the Indo-European base of facere is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 与 efficientia 均有记录，只有 facere 的印欧词基属于重构。

items.example: It is the base of the group.
It is the direct source noun.

definition_zh: 引语；引用；报价
definition_en: a group of words taken from a text or speech and repeated by someone else; the act of repeating such words; a price stated for goods or work
core_image: 一段被原样抄进新纸页的旧句子，句尾标着出处
scene: 论文的第一页上，作者把一段旧演讲原样抄下，并在句后标明出处。 The first page of the essay carries a quotation from an old speech.
sceneCN: 这里 quotation 是「引语」（第 1 个义项：从别处摘来并逐字重复的一段话）；句意为论文第一页引用了那段旧演讲中的一句话。画面里可留意：第一页、抄下的句子、句后的出处。

derivatives.zh: quotation 的动词原形，指引用或报价
quotable 加 -ity，指值得被引用的程度

senses.title: Words taken from another source
senses.definition: a passage repeated word for word from a book, speech or document
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或文件中逐字重复的一段话
senses.example: The essay opens with a quotation from an old speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以一段旧演讲的引语开头。
senses.why: Medieval Latin quotare meant to mark a text by numbers so passages could be cited, and the passage so marked became the quotation.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 quotare 意为给文本标号以便引证，被这样标出的一段话就成了 quotation。

senses.title: The act of repeating words
senses.definition: the act of repeating someone else's words, with or without credit
senses.definitionCN: 重复他人话语的行为，无论是否注明出处
senses.example: Quotation without credit is a form of theft.
senses.exampleCN: 不加注明地引用是一种剽窃。
senses.why: Once the noun named the copied passage, it also named the act of copying it, and the moral question of credit followed.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指抄下来的段落，也指抄写这一行为，随之而来的是「是否注明出处」的伦理问题。

senses.title: A stated price
senses.definition: a price given in advance for goods or for a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 为货物或某项工作预先给出的价格
senses.example: Ask the builder for a quotation before you agree.
senses.exampleCN: 答应之前先向施工方要一份报价。
senses.why: A trader who quotes a price marks it out in advance, and the same Latin verb of marking produced this commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 商人报出价格，就是把价格预先标定出来；同一个表示「标记」的拉丁语动词也生出了这层商业义。

intro.en: Quotation comes from a medieval Latin verb meaning to mark a book by numbers, built on the Latin word for how many, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: quotation 源自一个意为「给书编号」的中世纪拉丁语动词，其基础是拉丁语表示「多少」的词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quot was the Latin word for how many, used in phrases that numbered chapters and lines.
items.cn: quot 是拉丁语表示「多少」的词，用于给章节与诗行编号的说法。

items.en: Quotare meant to number the chapters of a book so that a passage could be pointed to precisely.
items.cn: quotare 意为给书的章节编号，以便精确指出某一段落。

items.en: The derived noun named the act of numbering, and by extension the passage marked with a number.
items.cn: 由其构成的名词指编号这一行为，并引申指标上了号码的那段文字。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where it came to mean the repeated passage itself.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，在英语里它转指被重复的那段文字本身。

items.en: Modern English uses quotation for cited words, for the act of citing them, and for a price stated in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quotation 指被引用的话、引用这一行为，以及预先报出的价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of numbering; the near-meaning group gathers words for cited passages and prices.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「编号」词干上的形式；近义组收表示被引段落与价格的词。

entries.definition: To repeat words or to state a price.
entries.definitionCN: 重复他人的话，或报出价格。

entries.definition: Worth being repeated in another text.
entries.definitionCN: 值得被别的文本引用的。

entries.definition: A fixed share of something allowed to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给某群体的固定份额。

entries.definition: The result of dividing one number by another.
entries.definitionCN: 一个数除以另一个数所得的结果。

entries.definition: A reference to a source, or words taken from it.
entries.definitionCN: 对来源的引用，或从来源中摘出的话。

entries.definition: A short passage taken from a longer work.
entries.definitionCN: 从较长作品中摘出的短段。

entries.definition: An approximate price or amount given in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 预先给出的约略价格或数量。

entries.definition: The amount of money asked for something.

normalIntro.en: The word began as numbering a text so a passage could be found, and the marked passage became the quotation we cite today.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「给文本编号以便找到某段」开始，被标出的段落就成了今天我们引用的 quotation。

normal.en: Quotation and quote share the Latin question how many, because early citations were marked with chapter numbers.
normal.cn: quotation 与 quote 共用拉丁语「多少」这一问，因为早期的引证靠章节编号来标记。

normal.en: Quotation marks are the written signs that enclose the borrowed words.
normal.cn: quotation marks 是围住借来之话的书写符号。

normal.en: A direct quotation repeats the exact words, while an indirect one reports their meaning without quotation marks.
normal.cn: 直接引语逐字重复原话，间接引语只转述意思而不用引号。

normal.en: A price quotation is the builder's way of quoting a figure before the work starts.
normal.cn: 报价（price quotation）是施工方在工作开始前报出数字的方式。

normal.en: Quotable means good enough to be repeated by other people.
normal.cn: quotable 意为好到值得被别人重复引用。

abstract.en: To quote is to let another voice speak inside your own sentence, and quotation marks mark the boundary of that borrowed voice.
abstract.cn: 引用就是让另一个声音在你的句子里说话，引号标出了这个借来之音的边界。

abstract.en: Every quotation is a small act of trust: the reader trusts that the words were really said or written.
abstract.cn: 每一次引用都是一次小小的信任行为：读者相信这些话确实被说过或写过。

abstract.en: The same word names a cited sentence and a price, because both are figures marked out in advance for others to accept.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指被引用的一句话，也指一个价格，因为两者都是预先标出、等待别人接受的数字。

examples.en: The report begins with a quotation from the mayor's speech.
examples.cn: 报告以市长演讲中的一段引语开头。

examples.en: Put the quotation in quotation marks and add the page number.
examples.cn: 把这段引语放进引号里，并补上页码。

examples.en: We accepted the quotation for the roof repair.
examples.cn: 我们接受了屋顶维修的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔贴身」——把别人的好句子阔气地贴在自己文章里，记得标出处，记住 quotation 是引语。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（给章节编号）→ quotationem → 法语 quotation → 英语 quotation；同族有 quote、quota、quotient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked passage; the senses divide into the cited words, the act of citing them and a price marked out in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被标出的段落」；义项分为被引用的文字、引用这一行为，以及预先标出的价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old sentence copied onto a fresh page, its source noted at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段旧句子被抄到新纸上，句末标着出处。

branches.en: a sentence in quotation marks
branches.cn: 放在引号里的一句话

branches.en: a pen copying a line by hand
branches.cn: 用手逐字抄下一行

branches.en: a figure written on a builder's letter
branches.cn: 写在施工方信函上的一个数字

branches.en: the borrowed words and the act of borrowing them
branches.cn: 借来的话与借这一动作

branches.en: the same marking done to a text and to a price
branches.cn: 同一种标记，一次标在文本上，一次标在价格上

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin question of how many, a verb of numbering, its noun of action and the French form that reached English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「多少」这一问、表示编号的动词、其动作名词，以及进入英语的法语形式构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quot is small but productive in English.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quot 的拉丁词群不大，却在英语里颇有生产力。

definition_zh: 收据；收到；配方
definition_en: a written proof of payment; the act of receiving; an old word for a recipe or formula
core_image: 一张薄纸从柜台递过来，上面印着金额
scene: 顾客把零钱收进钱包，店员递来一张打印的小票。 Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
sceneCN: 这里 receipt 是「收据」（第 1 个义项：付款的书面凭证）；句意为请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。画面里可留意：柜台递来的小票、打印的金额。

senses.title: A written proof of payment
senses.definition: a piece of paper that shows money or goods have been received
senses.definitionCN: 证明款项或货物已被收到的纸片
senses.example: Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
senses.exampleCN: 请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。
senses.why: The word began as the act of receiving and then came to name the paper that proves the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指「收到」这一行为，后来指证明该行为的纸片。

senses.title: The act of receiving
senses.definition: the act or fact of taking something that has been sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 接收已寄出或给予之物的行为或事实
senses.example: The receipt of the parcel was delayed by snow.
senses.exampleCN: 由于下雪，包裹的收取被延误了。
senses.why: Latin receptus, the past participle of recipere, named the act of taking something in, and English kept that abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 receptus 是 recipere 的过去分词，指「收进」这一行为，英语保留了这层抽象含义。

senses.title: An old word for a recipe
senses.definition: a written formula for preparing something, still used in pharmacy
senses.definitionCN: 制备某物的书面配方，药房仍在使用
senses.example: The old receipt for cough syrup is still in the family book.
senses.exampleCN: 那张治咳嗽糖浆的老配方还夹在家庭记事本里。
senses.why: Before recipe took over the kitchen, receipt named any written formula, and pharmacy kept the older word.
senses.whyCN: 在 recipe 接管厨房之前，receipt 指任何书面配方，药房一直保留这个更旧的词。

intro.en: Receipt begins as an act of taking, becomes a note about that act, and keeps an old sense of a written formula.
intro.cn: receipt 从「拿取」这一行为开始，变成关于该行为的字据，并保留了「书面配方」的旧义。

items.en: Recipere meant to take back or receive, built from re- and capere, to take.
items.cn: recipere 意为收回或接收，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Receptus, its past participle, named the thing or act received.
items.cn: 其过去分词 receptus 指被接收之物或接收这一行为。

items.en: Old French receite carried the word into English as a note of what was received.
items.cn: 古法语 receite 把这个词带入英语，指收到之物的字据。

items.en: English scholars later restored the silent p to honour the Latin root.
items.cn: 英语学者后来补回不发音的 p，以呼应拉丁词根。

items.en: Modern English uses receipt for proof of payment, for the act of receiving, and for an old formula.
items.cn: 现代英语用 receipt 指付款凭证、收取行为，也指旧式配方。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same long vowel; the near-meaning group gathers papers that record a transaction.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带长元音的词；近义组收记录交易的各类纸据。

entries.definition: A set of cooking instructions.
Deliberate deception.
Excessive self-pride.
A paper that can be exchanged for goods.
A bill listing goods and their price.
A small piece of paper.
A printed pass or token.

normalIntro.en: The word is a paper proof born from the act of receiving, with a silent p left over from Latin.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是由「收到」这一行为产生的纸面凭证，还留着从拉丁语来的不发音 p。

normal.en: The p in receipt is silent, so it sounds like re-seat.
normal.cn: receipt 里的 p 不发音，听起来像 re-seat。

normal.en: Keep the receipt is what a shop assistant says after payment.
normal.cn: Keep the receipt 是店员收款后常说的话。

normal.en: A receipt proves you paid; a recipe tells you how to cook.
normal.cn: receipt 证明你付过钱，recipe 告诉你怎样做菜。

normal.en: On receipt of means at the moment something arrives.
normal.cn: on receipt of 意为在某物到达的那一刻。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s, but the p stays silent.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s，但 p 依然不发音。

abstract.en: A receipt is trust made portable, a small proof you can carry away.
abstract.cn: 收据是可以带走的信任，是一份能随身携带的证明。

abstract.en: What is written down becomes a claim; what is not may be denied.
abstract.cn: 写下来的才成为凭据，没写下来的可能被否认。

abstract.en: Every receipt records a moment when two people agreed on a value.
abstract.cn: 每一张收据都记录着两个人就某个价值达成一致的瞬间。

examples.en: Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
examples.cn: 请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。

examples.en: The receipt of the parcel was delayed by snow.
examples.cn: 由于下雪，包裹的收取被延误了。

examples.en: The old receipt for cough syrup is still in the family book.
examples.cn: 那张治咳嗽糖浆的老配方还夹在家庭记事本里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「柜台递来一张纸」：付过钱，拿到凭证，就是收据；注意其中的 p 不发音。

root: 拉丁 recipere（收回、接收，re- 回 + capere 拿取）→ 拉丁 receptus → 古法语 receite → 英语 receipt（p 为后来按拉丁语复原的拼写）；同族有 receive、reception、recipient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking something in; the senses move from the act to the paper proof, and then to an old written formula.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西收进来」；义项从行为，到纸面凭证，再到旧式的书面配方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin slip of paper handed across a counter, the amount printed on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台那边递来一张薄纸，上面印着金额。

branches.en: a slip handed over the counter
branches.cn: 从柜台递过来的一张纸

branches.en: a parcel arriving at the door
branches.cn: 送到门口的包裹

branches.en: a formula written in an old book
branches.cn: 写在旧本子里的配方

branches.en: paper proof and the act it records
branches.cn: 纸面凭证与它所记录的行为

branches.en: receiving a note and receiving a formula
branches.cn: 收到字据，也收到配方

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin verb of taking, through a French note, and keeps a Latin spelling mark.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语的「拿取」动词，经法语的字据用法而来，并保留了一个拉丁拼写标记。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is recipere, with re- meaning back and capere meaning to take.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 recipere，其中 re- 意为「回」，capere 意为「拿取」。

definition_zh: 内心的；向内的；内部的
definition_en: directed towards the inside of something, or happening privately in the mind
core_image: 一支箭头从外面折回，指向自己胸口的方向
scene: 车窗外的城市飞速后退，他不再看风景，目光落在膝盖上的旧照片。 A long train ride always turns him inward.
sceneCN: 这里 inward 是「向内、转向内心」（第 2 个义项：注意力回到自己心里），句意为长途坐火车总让他转向内心。画面里的物件：车窗、旧照片、膝上的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：内心的；向内的；内部的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -s 构成，义为「向内地」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内心」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「内在性」
同构的相反词，义为「向外的」

senses.title: Pointing to the inside
senses.definition: facing or moving towards the centre of something
senses.definitionCN: 朝向或移向某物的中心
senses.example: The door opens with an inward swing.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门是向内开的。
senses.why: The suffix -weard marks the direction of a turn, as in forward.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -weard 标出转身的方向，正如 forward。

senses.title: Turned to the mind
senses.definition: directed at your own thoughts and feelings rather than at the world outside
senses.definitionCN: 指向自己内心的想法与感受，而非外部世界
senses.example: Her inward life was far busier than her quiet days suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 她的内心生活远比表面安静的日子忙碌。
senses.why: The same arrow was turned from rooms to feelings by later writers.
senses.whyCN: 后世的写作者把同一支箭头从房间转向了感受。

senses.title: Inside a body or building
senses.definition: situated on the inside part of a body or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于身体或建筑结构内侧的
senses.example: The inward wall was damp after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，内墙是潮的。
senses.why: In building and anatomy the word stays physical and means the inner face.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑与解剖里这个词仍指实物，意为内侧的那一面。

intro.en: Inward is a native English compound: the preposition in plus the old suffix -weard, "turned towards".
intro.cn: inward 是英语本土的复合词：介词 in 加上古词尾 -weard「朝向」。

items.en: The word innan meant "within".
items.cn: 古英语 innan 意为「在里面」。

items.en: The suffix -weard meant "turned towards", as in toward.
items.cn: 词尾 -weard 意为「朝向」，与 toward 同源。

items.en: inweard joined them: turned towards the inside.
items.cn: inweard 把两者合起：朝向内的一面。

items.en: Middle English kept inward for the body and the spirit alike.
items.cn: 中古英语用 inward 兼指身体与心灵。

items.en: Modern English added the -ly adverb to mark the mental sense.
items.cn: 现代英语加 -ly 副词来标出心理义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ward direction suffix; the near-meaning group holds words for the inner world.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ward 方向词尾；近义组收表示内在世界的词。

entries.definition: Turned towards the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「向外的」，镜像词。

entries.definition: The adverb form, moving to the inside.
The one nearer the centre.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，强调位置。

entries.definition: Happening inside a thing or body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的」，偏客观。

entries.definition: Kept to oneself, not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「私人的」，偏不公开。

entries.definition: Habitually looking into one's own mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内省的」，偏习惯。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rely on the -ward ending you already know from forward.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子靠的是你从 forward 里已经认识的 -ward。

normal.en: in plus ward means turned towards the inside.
normal.cn: in 加 ward 就是朝向里面。

normal.en: Forward goes ahead, inward goes in.
normal.cn: forward 向前，inward 向内。

normal.en: An inward door swings into the room.
normal.cn: 向内开的门是朝房间里面转。

normal.en: Its mirror is outward, with the same ending.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 outward，词尾一样。

normal.en: Turn it on feelings and it means private thought.
normal.cn: 把它对准感受，就指私下的思绪。

abstract.en: Inward is the compass that points at yourself.
abstract.cn: inward 是指向自己的那只罗盘。

abstract.en: Every journey out has a matching journey in.
abstract.cn: 每一趟向外的行程都配一趟向内。

abstract.en: A quiet face can hide the busiest room.
abstract.cn: 安静的脸可以藏住最忙的房间。

examples.en: He gave an inward sigh and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他在心里叹了口气，什么也没说。

examples.en: The inward curve of the bay shelters small boats.
examples.cn: 海湾向内弯，护住了小船。

examples.en: Years of inward reflection made him a patient listener.
examples.cn: 多年的内省使他成了有耐心的倾听者。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ ward（朝向）——朝里面去的

root: 古英语 in「内」+ -weard「朝向」→ inweard → 中古英语 inward。同族有 inwards、inwardly、inwardness；反义 outward。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: pointing inside, turned to the mind, and on the inner side of a body or wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：指向内部、转向内心，以及位于身体或墙的内侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow bent back towards its own chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支折回自己胸口的箭头。

branches.en: THE DOOR: an opening that swings into the room.
branches.cn: 门这条线：朝房间里面转开的入口。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention folded back on itself.
branches.cn: 心灵这条线：注意力折回自身。

branches.en: THE WALL: the side of a structure facing the middle.
branches.cn: 墙这条线：朝向中心的那个面。

branches.en: THE SPACE: both senses are about position and direction.
branches.cn: 空间这条线：两个义项都是位置与方向。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN: what faces inward is not on show.
branches.cn: 隐藏这条线：朝向内侧的东西都不外露。

intro.en: Inward is in- plus the Old English direction suffix -weard.
intro.cn: inward 是 in- 加古英语方向词尾 -weard。

latinIntro.en: This word is native Germanic, so latinEntries stays empty; the Latin cousin is internus.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本土词，所以 latinEntries 留空；拉丁语里的表亲是 internus。

items.example: It also builds forward and backward.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 forward 与 backward。

items.example: It makes the mirror word outward.
A related form with the same in sense.
A comparative built on the same root.

definition_zh: 磁铁；磁石；有吸引力的人或地方
definition_en: an object that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field, or a person or place that draws others
core_image: 一块黑亮的石头压在铁钉堆上，钉子像树枝一样从它身上长出来
scene: 厨房里，孩子把一张画纸吸在冰箱门上，纸没有掉下来，门上还挂着一串回形针。 A small magnet holds the drawing while the fridge door swings open.
sceneCN: 这里 magnet 指「能吸铁的磁体」（第 2 个义项：人造的小块磁铁）；句意为一块小磁铁吸住画纸，冰箱门打开时纸也没掉。图中可辨识物件：冰箱门、画纸、彩色磁贴、回形针；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有吸引力的人；吸引人群的地方

derivatives.zh: 磁的；有磁性的；有吸引力的

senses.title: The natural stone
senses.definition: a piece of naturally magnetized iron ore that attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 天然带磁性的铁矿石，能吸铁
senses.example: The old compass held a sliver of magnet cut from native ore.
senses.exampleCN: 那只旧罗盘里装着一小片从天然矿石上切下来的磁石。
senses.why: Before manufacture, the word meant the ore itself: a stone found already able to move iron.
senses.whyCN: 在人工制造出现之前，这个词指的就是矿石本身：一块被发现时就已经能移动铁的石头。

senses.title: A shaped piece of magnetized metal
senses.titleCN: 人造磁铁：加工成形的磁体
senses.definition: a piece of metal or ceramic made so that it attracts iron
senses.definitionCN: 经过加工、能吸铁的金属或陶瓷块
senses.example: He stuck the note to the fridge with a small magnet.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一块小磁铁把便条贴在冰箱上。
senses.why: The same power found in ore can be shaped into bars and discs, so the noun widened from a found stone to a made tool.
senses.whyCN: 矿石里的那种力量可以被加工成条块与圆片，于是这个名词从捡到的石头扩大到做出来的工具。

senses.title: A coil with an iron core
senses.titleCN: 电磁铁：靠电流工作的磁体
senses.definition: a coil of wire with an iron core that acts as a magnet while current flows
senses.definitionCN: 通电时起磁体作用的带铁芯线圈
senses.example: The crane's magnet releases the scrap metal when the current stops.
senses.exampleCN: 电流一断，吊车的电磁铁就把废金属放开。
senses.why: Once electricity could make magnetism, a magnet no longer had to be a permanent stone; it could be switched on and off.
senses.whyCN: 当电能够制造磁性，磁体就不必再是永久的石头，而可以被开与关。

senses.title: The two poles of a magnet
senses.definition: one of the two ends of a magnet, where the pull is strongest and opposite poles attract
senses.definitionCN: 磁体两端吸力最强之处，异极相吸、同极相斥
senses.example: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, however often it is cut.
senses.exampleCN: 无论把磁铁切多少次，每一块都仍有南极和北极。
senses.why: The object is not uniform: the pull concentrates at the ends, and that pair of ends is part of what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 物体并不均匀：吸力集中在两端，而这一对端点也是这个词所指内容的一部分。

senses.title: A charming person
senses.definition: a person who attracts others strongly, as if by magnetism
senses.definitionCN: 像被磁力吸引那样强烈吸引他人的人
senses.example: As a speaker she was a magnet, and the hall filled within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 作为演讲者，她像一块磁石，几分钟就把礼堂填满了。
senses.why: A stone that draws iron is an easy picture for a person who draws a crowd, so the noun moved from metal to people.
senses.whyCN: 吸铁的石头很容易拿来比喻吸住人群的人，于是这个名词从金属转到了人。

senses.title: A place that draws visitors
senses.definition: a place that attracts many visitors or residents
senses.definitionCN: 吸引大量游客或居民的地方
senses.example: The rebuilt pier became a magnet for day trippers.
senses.exampleCN: 重建后的码头成了当日游客的聚集地。
senses.why: A place pulls people the way the stone pulls iron: no one orders the crowd to come, yet the current of visitors bends toward it.
senses.whyCN: 地方吸人就像磁石吸铁：没有人下令，游客的人流却朝它弯过去。

senses.title: A centre that draws resources
senses.titleCN: 吸引人才与资金的中心
senses.definition: an institution or district that draws talent, money or investment
senses.definitionCN: 吸引人才、资金或投资的机构或地区
senses.example: The research park is a magnet for young engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座研究园区是年轻工程师的聚集地。
senses.why: The metaphor turns practical: a place that offers work and equipment draws skilled people and their money as reliably as a field draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转为实用：一个提供工作与设备的地方，吸来技术人才与资金，其可靠程度如同磁场吸铁。

senses.title: Anything that captures attention
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：吸引注意力的事物
senses.definition: anything that holds attention so firmly that people turn to it
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住注意力、让人转向它的事物
senses.example: That question acted as a magnet for the whole debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题像磁石一样吸住了整场辩论。
senses.why: The pull can attach to nothing physical at all: an idea holds attention the way a stone holds filings, and the noun needs no metal.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力完全可以不附着在任何实物上：一个念头抓住注意，就像石头抓住铁屑，这个名词不再需要金属。

intro.en: Magnet comes from the Greek name of the stone of Magnesia through Latin and Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnet 经拉丁语与古法语，上溯希腊语中「马格尼西亚的石头」之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, the stone of Magnesia, named a natural iron ore that already attracted iron. The place-name account is generally accepted; the origin of the place name is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 即「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种本身就能吸铁的天然矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的；地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and used it for the ore and for anything that behaved like it.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊名词作 magnes，属格 magnetis，既指矿石，也指任何行为像它的东西。

items.en: Old French magnete carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, at first as the name of the mineral.
items.cn: 古法语 magnete 在十三世纪把这个词带进英语，最初是矿物的名字。

items.en: Experimenters began shaping iron into artificial magnets, and the word widened from a found stone to any made object with the same power.
items.cn: 实验者开始把铁加工成人造磁体，这个词也从「捡到的石头」扩大到任何具有同样力量的制成品。

items.en: In 1825 William Sturgeon wrapped a coil around an iron core and called it an electromagnet, tying the noun to a switchable device.
items.cn: 1825 年斯特金把线圈绕在铁芯上，称之为电磁铁，把这个名词与可开关的装置绑在一起。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries a magnet was also a person or place that draws others, especially visitors, talent or money.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，magnet 也指吸引他人的人或地方，尤其吸引游客、人才或资金。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same stem and one look-alike from another root; group two holds things that attract in the same practical way.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词干的词，以及一个异源形近词；第二组是在实际用途上同样能吸引东西的事物。

entries.definition: Describes what a magnet is or does; the noun names the object.
entries.definitionCN: 形容磁体是什么、能做什么；名词则指物件。

entries.definition: The property or the science; a magnet is the thing that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 性质或学科；magnet 是拥有这一性质的东西。

entries.definition: The black mineral that magnets are made from and that occurs naturally magnetized.
entries.definitionCN: 可用来制作磁体、也会天然带磁的黑色矿物。

entries.definition: A business magnate, from Latin magnus 'great'; it is not related to the stone at all.
entries.definitionCN: 商业巨头，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；与磁石毫无同源关系。

entries.definition: The old name for naturally magnetized magnetite, the original magnet.
entries.definitionCN: 天然带磁的磁铁矿的旧称，也就是最早的磁石。

entries.definition: A magnet that works only while current flows, so it can be turned off.
entries.definitionCN: 只在通电时起作用的磁体，因此可以关掉。

entries.definition: Any drawing force; a magnet is one physical source of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何拉力；磁体是它在物理上的一种来源。

entries.definition: The act of pulling a crowd or interest; a magnet is the object that produces the draw.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人群或兴趣的动作；magnet 是产生这种吸引的物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stone name, the real compounds and the real modern metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的石名、真实的复合词，以及真实存在的现代比喻。

normal.en: The word is the stone, not the property: magnet names the thing, magnetism names what it has.
normal.cn: 这个词指的是石头而非性质：magnet 指物件，magnetism 指它拥有的东西。

normal.en: Everyday magnets carry prefixes: electromagnet, nanomagnet, fridge magnet.
normal.cn: 日常磁体常带前缀：电磁铁、纳米磁体、冰箱贴。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the figurative sense: a magnet for tourists, a magnet for talent, a magnet school.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示比喻义：吸引游客的地方、吸引人才的中心、特色择优学校。

normal.en: The same stone name gives magnetite, the ore, and magnetometer, the measuring device.
normal.cn: 同一个石名还给出 magnetite（矿石）与 magnetometer（测量器械）。

normal.en: Cut a magnet in half and you do not get one pole; you get two smaller magnets, each with both poles.
normal.cn: 把磁铁切成两半，你不会得到一个单极，而是得到两块更小的磁铁，各有两极。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that grows iron branches when it is laid on a pile of nails.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头放在钉堆上，就长出铁的枝条。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that turns attraction on and off without moving the metal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关，不动金属就能让吸引力出现或消失。

abstract.en: Picture a town where every road seems to slope gently toward the same square.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇，每条路都像微微向下倾向同一个广场。

examples.en: A magnet is useless once it is heated far above its working temperature.
examples.cn: 磁铁被加热到远超工作温度之后就没用了。

examples.en: The festival has become a magnet for young filmmakers.
examples.cn: 这个影展已经成了年轻电影人的聚集地。

examples.en: She kept the spare key under a magnet on the steel door.
examples.cn: 她把备用钥匙放在钢门上的磁贴下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 马格内特——来自马格尼西亚的石头，能吸铁 → 磁石、磁铁

root: 希腊 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚石）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 古法语 magnete → 英语 magnet。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the native ore and the shaped object, then its poles and its electric version, and end with the person, place and idea that draw others.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天然矿石与成形磁体出发，经过两极与电磁版本，最后落到吸人的人、地方与念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black stone with iron nails growing out of it like branches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑石头上长出铁钉，像树枝一样。

branches.en: Found stone and made object: the same power, first in ore and then in a shaped piece.
branches.cn: 捡来的石头与制成的物件：同一种力量，先在矿石里，后在成形块里。

branches.en: A magnet can be switched by current, and every version still has two poles.
branches.cn: 磁体可由电流开关，而无论哪种版本都仍有两极。

branches.en: The stone's pull applied to a person who holds a room.
branches.cn: 磁石的拉力用在一个人身上，他能稳住一屋子人。

branches.en: A place or an institution that pulls visitors, talent and money.
branches.cn: 一个地方或机构，吸来游客、人才与资金。

branches.en: The pull detached from place and metal, working on attention itself.
branches.cn: 拉力脱离地方与金属，直接作用于注意力。

intro.en: Magnet is a free noun from Greek through Latin, and all its relatives attach ordinary suffixes to that stem.
intro.cn: magnet 是经拉丁语来自希腊语的自由名词，所有亲属词都在这同一词干上加普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, is the direct source; magnetismus is a New Latin extension, and Greek magnēs stands at the head of the chain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）是直接来源；magnetismus 是新拉丁语的延伸，链条最前端是希腊 magnēs。

items.example: The magnet clung to the steel frame.

items.meaning: having the power of a magnet
items.meaningCN: 有磁性的（加形容词后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic clamp held the plate.

items.meaningCN: 磁性（加状态后缀，物件转为性质）
items.example: Magnetism faded as the metal cooled.

items.meaning: to make an object act like a magnet
items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加使动后缀，性质被赋予别的物件）
items.example: A brief pulse magnetizes the needle.
items.exampleCN: 一次短脉冲就能使指针磁化。

items.meaning: the process or strength of being magnetized
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化强度（再加过程后缀）
items.exampleCN: 跌落之后磁化状态仍在。

items.meaning: the black ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由物件转为矿种）
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿颗粒把沙子染黑。

items.meaning: a magnet driven by a coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（电加磁体，动力来源变成电流）
items.example: The electromagnet lifts the car bodies.

items.meaning: a small decorative magnet for a refrigerator
items.meaningCN: 冰箱贴（由冰箱与磁体复合，用途收窄到装饰）
items.example: She bought a fridge magnet at the museum.
items.exampleCN: 她在博物馆买了一个冰箱贴。

latinEntries.meaning: the region behind the stone's name

definition_zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的
definition_en: belonging to an early stage of development; simple or basic rather than advanced
core_image: 一根削尖的树枝与一块打制的石片，旁边摆着一台精密仪器，两者对照出「最初的样子」
scene: 展柜里，削尖的树枝与打制石片被标为最初阶段，旁边是一台精密仪器。 A primitive toolkit of sharpened sticks and knapped stone lay beside a precision instrument.
sceneCN: 这里 primitive 指「属于最早阶段的、未加工的」（第 1 个义项：原始的、早期的）；句意为展柜里一套削尖树枝与打制石片的原始工具放在精密仪器旁边。可辨识物件：树枝、石片、展柜、仪器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的；原始派的

derivatives.zh: primitive（原始的）+ -ly（古英语 -līce，方式副词）→ 原始地；简陋地
primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋
primitive（原始的）+ -ism（拉丁 -ismus，主义）→ 原始主义
primitive（原始的）+ art（艺术）→ 原始派艺术
primitive（原始的）+ -ist（主义者）→ 原始主义者

senses.title: Belonging to the earliest stage
senses.definition: belonging to an early stage of development, before refinement
senses.definitionCN: 属于发展的早期阶段，尚未精细化
senses.example: Primitive tools were made by striking one stone against another.
senses.exampleCN: 原始工具是把一块石头往另一块上打制而成的。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin primus 'first', so its core sense is simply 'of the first stage'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由拉丁 primus「第一」构成，核心义就是「属于第一阶段」。

senses.title: Simple and rough
senses.definition: simple to the point of being uncomfortable or inadequate
senses.definitionCN: 简单到令人不适或不够用的程度
senses.example: The camp had only primitive washing facilities.
senses.exampleCN: 营地只有极为简陋的洗浴设施。
senses.why: Because early stages lack refinement, 'first' easily slides into 'rough' when applied to living conditions.
senses.whyCN: 由于早期阶段缺少打磨，「第一」用于生活条件时很容易滑向「粗糙」。

senses.title: A dated word for peoples
senses.titleCN: 未开化的（旧用法，含贬义）
senses.definition: an old and now discredited label for peoples considered less advanced
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对被视为不发达民族的一种标签，如今已被否定且含贬义
senses.example: Nineteenth-century writers used primitive in ways that modern anthropology rejects.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪作者使用 primitive 的方式，现代人类学已予否定。
senses.why: The label assumed a single ladder of progress, and the word inherited that assumption.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签预设了一条单一的进步阶梯，词义也继承了这一预设。

senses.title: Undeveloped in biology
senses.definition: in an early or undifferentiated form, as a cell or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 处于早期或未分化状态，如细胞或组织
senses.example: The embryo's primitive streak marks the first axis of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎的原条标出身体的第一条轴线。
senses.why: Biology uses 'first-stage' literally: the structure appears before its later specializations.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把「第一阶段」用得很实：该结构出现在后来的特化之前。

senses.title: Taken as basic in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与数学中的初始的
senses.definition: accepted without definition, as a starting notion in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统中作为起点而不加定义地接受
senses.example: Point and line are primitive notions in that geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 在那套几何里，点与线是初始概念。
senses.why: A primitive notion is one you cannot derive, so the word keeps its 'first' sense exactly.
senses.whyCN: 初始概念是无法推导的东西，因此这个词精确保留了「第一」义。

senses.title: Art outside the academic tradition
senses.definition: art by self-taught makers or from traditions outside formal training
senses.definitionCN: 自学作者或学院传统之外的艺术
senses.example: The exhibition placed primitive art beside trained portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把原始派艺术与受过训练的人像画并置。
senses.why: Collectors used the word for work they saw as untrained, and the label survived in art history.
senses.whyCN: 收藏家用这个词指他们眼中未受训练的作品，这个标签在艺术史中保留下来。

senses.title: A self-taught painter's style
senses.definition: a style marked by flat perspective and strong outline
senses.definitionCN: 以平面透视与强烈轮廓为特征的风格
senses.example: The primitive painter filled the canvas with flat houses and bright roofs.
senses.exampleCN: 这位自学画家在画布上排满平面房屋和鲜艳屋顶。
senses.why: The style sense comes from the makers rather than the period, so a modern untrained painter can still be called primitive.
senses.whyCN: 风格义来自作者而非年代，因此现代的自学画家仍可被称为原始派。

senses.title: A root word in linguistics
senses.definition: a word that is not derived from another word in the same language
senses.definitionCN: 在同一语言中不由别的词派生的词
senses.example: Hand is a primitive word, while handful is derived.
senses.exampleCN: 「手」是词根词，而由它加后缀构成的「一把之量」是派生词。
senses.why: Linguistics borrows the 'first' sense: the word stands at the base of a derivational family.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了「第一」义：这个词位于一个派生词族的基底。

intro.en: Primitive comes from Latin primus 'first' through the derived adjective primitivus and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: primitive 来自拉丁 primus「第一」，经派生形容词 primitivus 与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Primus meant 'first'; it also gives prime, primary, primate and primal, so the family is large.
items.cn: primus 意为「第一」，也产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal，因此词族很大。

items.en: Primitivus meant 'first of its kind, earliest', built from primus plus the adjective ending -ivus.
items.cn: primitivus 意为「同类中最早的」，由 primus 加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。

items.en: Old French primitif carried the adjective into English in the fifteenth century, first in religious language.
items.cn: 古法语 primitif 在 15 世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于宗教语言。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was used for art outside academic training and for peoples judged less advanced, a use now rejected.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个词被用于学院训练之外的艺术，也被用于被判定为不发达的民族，后者如今已被否定。

items.en: Biology and logic kept the literal 'first' sense: a primitive structure or notion is one that comes before the rest.
items.cn: 生物学与逻辑学保留了字面的「第一」义：初始结构或初始概念都先于其余部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the Indo-European root behind primus is reconstructed as per 'forward, before', a reconstruction and not a recorded form; the fifteenth-century English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：primus 之前的印欧词根被重构为 per「向前、在前」，属重构形式而非有记录的形式；英语 15 世纪的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin 'first' root with different ranks; group two holds near meanings that describe stage or finish.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「第一」词根、但等级不同的词；第二组是描述阶段或完成度的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin primus 'first'; it means first in importance or the best period, not earliest in time.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primus「第一」；指地位首要或全盛期，而非时间上最早。

entries.definition: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank'; it means first in order or basic.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primarius「居首的」；指次序第一或基础性的。

entries.definition: From Latin primas 'of the first rank'; the animal order was named as the 'first' order by Linnaeus.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primas「居首位的」；动物目名是林奈把它列为「第一」目而来。

entries.definition: From primus plus -al; it stresses what is earliest and most instinctive.
entries.definitionCN: 由 primus 加 -al 构成；强调最早、最本能的部分。

entries.definition: Simply first in time, with no judgment about refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指时间上早，不含精细程度的判断。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, often implying poor workmanship rather than an early stage.
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙未加工，常指做工差，而非发展阶段早。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation, with no suggestion of being outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的，不含过时之意。

entries.definition: Not yet grown or elaborated, used of land, ideas or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成长或展开，用于土地、想法或生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real primus family and the scientific senses that keep 'first' literally.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 primus 词族，以及保留字面「第一」的科学义项。

normal.en: Latin primus 'first' gives prime, primary, primate and primal.
normal.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal。

normal.en: The comparative is more primitive, not primitiver.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more primitive，不写作 primitiver。

normal.en: Biology keeps 'first' literally in primitive streak and primitive cell.
normal.cn: 生物学在「原条」「原初细胞」中保留字面的「第一」。

normal.en: Logic uses primitive notion for a starting idea taken without definition.
normal.cn: 逻辑学用 primitive notion 指不加定义的初始概念。

normal.en: The anthropological label is now avoided in careful writing.
normal.cn: 人类学的旧标签如今在严谨写作中已被避免。

abstract.en: Picture a sharpened stick lying beside a polished instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象一根削尖的树枝躺在一台光亮的仪器旁。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing with a flat sky and a bright roof, made by someone who never trained.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅天空扁平的画，屋顶鲜亮，出自从未受过训练的人之手。

abstract.en: Picture a first step on a staircase whose top you cannot yet see.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯的第一级，顶端还看不见。

examples.en: The primitive plough was no more than a pointed branch.
examples.cn: 原始犁不过是一根削尖的树枝。

examples.en: The village had primitive drainage and no running water.
examples.cn: 这个村子排水简陋，也没有自来水。

examples.en: Point and line are primitive notions in the system.
examples.cn: 点与线在该系统中是初始概念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pri（第一）＋mitive」——排在第一、最早的样子 → 原始的

root: 拉丁 primus「第一」+ 形容词词尾 -ivus 构成 primitivus「同类中最早的」，经古法语 primitif 入英语；primus 之前的印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the literal first stage, then move to rough conditions, the discredited label for peoples, undifferentiated biology, logic that takes its starting notions without definition, art outside training, a self-taught style and a root word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的第一阶段出发，随后是简陋条件、已被否定的民族标签、未分化的生物结构、不加定义的逻辑起点、学院外的艺术、自学画风与词根词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharpened stick beside a precision instrument, the first step before the polished one.
core.cn: 核心意象：削尖树枝与精密仪器并置，光洁之前的第一级台阶。

branches.en: FIRST STAGE: what comes earliest is also what lacks finish.
branches.cn: 第一阶段：最先出现的也往往最缺打磨。

branches.en: REJECTED LABEL: the old word for peoples rested on a false ladder.
branches.cn: 被否定的标签：旧时对民族的称法建立在虚假的阶梯上。

branches.en: LITERAL FIRST: biology and logic keep the sense of what comes before the rest.
branches.cn: 字面的第一：生物学与逻辑学保留「先于其余」之义。

branches.en: UNTAUGHT ART: makers outside training are named by their distance from the academy.
branches.cn: 未受训的艺术：学院之外的作者以其距离学院而得名。

branches.en: ROOT WORD: the base of a derivational family is 'first' again.
branches.cn: 词根词：派生词族的基底又回到了「第一」。

intro.en: Primitive belongs to the large Latin primus family, and its prefixes and suffixes show how 'first' branches into rank, time and foundation.
intro.cn: primitive 属于庞大的拉丁 primus 词族，其词缀显示「第一」如何分出等级、时间与基础三层。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus 'first' gives primitivus, primarius, primas and primal; the English endings -ly, -ness and -ism build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 primitivus、primarius、primas 与 primal；英语后缀 -ly、-ness 与 -ism 构成其余部分。

items.example: Primus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: primus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The Latin adjective passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词经法语传来。

items.example: A primitive tool needs no finishing.
The primitiveness of the camp surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 营地的简陋让他们吃惊。
原始主义影响了早期现代绘画。

items.meaning: first in rank or the best period

items.example: The primate is our closest relative among mammals.
items.exampleCN: 灵长类是哺乳动物中与我们最近的亲属。

latinEntries.structure: primus, prima, primum (adj., first and second declension)
primitivus, primitiva, primitivum (adj., first and second declension)

derivatives.zh: primitive（原始的）+ -ly（古英语 -līce，方式副词）→ 原始地；简陋地
primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋
primitive（原始的）+ -ism（拉丁 -ismus，主义）→ 原始主义
primitive（原始的）+ art（艺术）→ 原始派艺术
primitive（原始的）+ -ist（主义者）→ 原始主义者

definition_zh: 敌对的；不友善的；敌方的
definition_en: unfriendly and ready to oppose or attack
core_image: 两群人隔着栅栏怒目相视，气氛紧张
scene: 人群对这项计划抱有敌意。 The crowd was hostile to the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 hostile 是「敌对的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人群对这项计划抱有敌意。

senses.title: Unfriendly and opposed
senses.definition: showing strong dislike and opposition
senses.definitionCN: 表现出强烈反感的
senses.example: The crowd was hostile to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 人群对这项计划抱有敌意。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of unfriendly opposition.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常所说的不友善的反对。

senses.title: Of an enemy or harsh place
senses.definition: belonging to an enemy or being difficult to survive in
senses.definitionCN: 属于敌人或难以生存的
senses.example: The soldiers entered hostile territory.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们进入了敌方领土。
senses.why: Here the word describes an enemy or a harsh setting.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述敌人或严酷的环境。

intro.en: Hostile comes from the Latin word for an enemy.
intro.cn: hostile 来自拉丁语中表示敌人的词。

items.en: Hostis meant an enemy or stranger.
items.cn: hostis 意为敌人或陌生人。

items.en: Hostilis meant of an enemy.
items.cn: hostilis 意为敌人的。

items.en: Hostile carried the sense of enemy opposition.
items.cn: hostile 带有敌人对抗的含义。

items.en: Hostile described enemy forces and feelings.
items.cn: hostile 描述敌军与敌意。

items.en: Hostile now also describes harsh conditions.
items.cn: hostile 现在也描述严酷的条件。

note.en: Hostile is compared with look-alike words and with words for unfriendliness.
note.cn: 把 hostile 与形近词以及表示不友善的词作比较。

entries.definition: a simple place to stay
unfriendly feeling
a place of medical care
not kind or welcoming
ready to attack
showing active opposition

normalIntro.en: Hostile describes an attitude or place that opposes and threatens.
normalIntro.cn: hostile 描述充满对抗与威胁的态度或环境。

normal.en: The crowd was hostile to the plan.
normal.cn: 人群对这项计划抱有敌意。

normal.en: His hostile tone ended the conversation.
normal.cn: 他敌对的语气结束了谈话。

normal.en: The soldiers entered hostile territory.
normal.cn: 士兵们进入了敌方领土。

normal.en: The company fought off a hostile takeover.
normal.cn: 公司击退了一次恶意收购。

normal.en: Plants struggle in such a hostile climate.
normal.cn: 植物在如此恶劣的气候中难以生长。

abstract.en: Hostile turns a stranger into an enemy in one small step.
abstract.cn: hostile 让陌生人只差一小步就变成敌人。

abstract.en: A hostile place is one that does not want you to stay.
abstract.cn: 敌对环境就是不愿让你留下的地方。

abstract.en: The word measures distance: how far another person stands from us.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量距离：他人离我们有多远。

examples.en: The crowd was hostile to the plan.
examples.cn: 人群对这项计划抱有敌意。

examples.en: The soldiers entered hostile territory.
examples.cn: 士兵们进入了敌方领土。

examples.en: Plants struggle in such a hostile climate.
examples.cn: 植物在如此恶劣的气候中难以生长。

dict_mnemonic.text: hostile 源自拉丁语 hostis（敌人），所以既指「敌对的」，也指「敌方的、恶劣的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 hostis（敌人）与形容词 hostilis，经法语 hostile 进入英语，核心是敌对与对抗。

sensesIntro.en: Hostile means unfriendly and opposed, or belonging to an enemy and hard to endure.
sensesIntro.cn: hostile 表示不友善、对抗的，也表示敌方的、难以忍受的。

core.en: An attitude or place that stands against you.
core.cn: 与你对立的态度或环境。

branches.en: The crowd was hostile to the plan.
branches.cn: 人群对这项计划抱有敌意。

branches.en: His hostile tone ended the conversation.
branches.cn: 他敌对的语气结束了谈话。

branches.en: The soldiers entered hostile territory.
branches.cn: 士兵们进入了敌方领土。

branches.en: A hostile feeling and a hostile land share one word.
branches.cn: 敌对情绪与敌对环境共用一个词。

branches.en: Plants struggle in such a hostile climate.
branches.cn: 植物在如此恶劣的气候中难以生长。

intro.en: Hostile forms the noun hostility and the adverb hostilely.
intro.cn: hostile 可构成名词 hostility 与副词 hostilely。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hostis also underlies host and hostel, though the senses drifted apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hostis 也是 host 与 hostel 的来源，只是词义逐渐分化。

items.example: We thanked them for their hospitality.

latinEntries.example: Hostis is the root of hostile.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hostis 是 hostile 的词根。

definition_zh: 组成；构成；创作；使镇静
definition_en: to form something by putting parts together, or to write music or a letter
core_image: 一个人把散落的音符一个个摆上五线谱
scene: 演出前，作曲家在后台安静地写完最后一段旋律。 She needed a quiet room to compose the final movement.
sceneCN: 这里 compose 指「创作乐曲」（第 2 个义项：写音乐或文章）；句意是她需要一个安静的房间来写最后一个乐章。

senses.title: Put parts into a whole
senses.definition: to combine parts so that they form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分组合起来形成一个整体
senses.example: Ten chapters compose the whole book.
senses.exampleCN: 十个章节构成整本书。
senses.why: The parts come first, and the whole appears only when they are placed together.
senses.whyCN: 部分先存在，只有把它们放在一起，整体才出现。

senses.title: Write music or text
senses.definition: to write music, a poem or a letter
senses.definitionCN: 创作音乐、诗歌或书信
senses.example: He composed the song in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 他一夜之间写成了这首歌。
senses.why: Notes and words are also parts, and the writer places them in order.
senses.whyCN: 音符和文字也是部分，作者把它们按顺序摆好。

senses.title: Calm yourself down
senses.definition: to make yourself calm after strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 在强烈情绪之后使自己平静下来
senses.example: She took a breath to compose herself.
senses.exampleCN: 她吸了一口气让自己镇定下来。
senses.why: To compose the mind is to put its scattered parts back in order.
senses.whyCN: 整理心绪，就是把散乱的部分重新放回秩序里。

intro.en: Compose comes from Latin componere, to put together, and reached English through Old French composer.
intro.cn: compose 来自拉丁语 componere（放在一起），经古法语 composer 进入英语。

items.en: Componere joined com-, together, with ponere, to put.
items.cn: componere 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）组合而成。

items.en: Compositus described something neatly arranged from parts.
items.cn: compositus 描述由各部分整齐组合而成的东西。

items.en: Old French composer meant to put in order or to settle.
items.cn: 古法语 composer 意为整理、安排或平息。

items.en: English compose first meant to arrange or to form from parts.
items.cn: 英语 compose 最初指安排或由部分组成。

items.en: It grew to cover writing music and calming the mind.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到创作音乐与平复心绪。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to compose, and the meaning group names other ways of putting a whole together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compose 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他把整体拼起来的说法。

entries.definition: to consist of particular parts
decayed plant material used to feed soil
a calm and controlled state of mind
to make something new
to put things in a neat order
to make or shape something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with parts laid on a desk, then move to music and to a mind put back in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从摊在桌上的部分开始，再走到音乐与重新整理好的心绪。

normal.en: Com- is together and pos- is put, so compose is to put things together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pos- 是放置，compose 就是把东西放到一起。

normal.en: A composer puts notes together the way a builder puts bricks together.
normal.cn: 作曲家摆放音符，就像砌工摆放砖块。

normal.en: Be composed of means the parts are already in place.
normal.cn: be composed of 表示各部分已经放好。

normal.en: Compose yourself is to gather your scattered feelings.
normal.cn: compose yourself 就是把自己散乱的情绪收拢起来。

normal.en: A composed person looks as if everything is in its place.
normal.cn: 一个 composed 的人，看上去一切各就各位。

abstract.en: Picture a hand setting each chess piece on its square.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把每枚棋子放上它的格子。

abstract.en: Picture five lines of music slowly filling with notes.
abstract.cn: 想象五行乐谱慢慢被音符填满。

abstract.en: Picture a messy desk sorted into neat piles.
abstract.cn: 想象一张乱桌被整理成整齐的几摞。

examples.en: Ten small states compose the whole union.
examples.cn: 十个小州组成整个联邦。

examples.en: She composed the letter carefully before sending it.
examples.cn: 她仔细写好信才寄出去。

examples.en: He paused to compose himself before speaking.
examples.cn: 他停顿一下让自己镇定，然后才开口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compose 记成 com（一起）加 pose（摆放）：把各部分摆到一起，就是组成，也可以指作曲。

root: 源自拉丁语 componere（com 一起 + ponere 放置），本义是放在一起，后引申为组成、创作与使心绪安定。

sensesIntro.en: From parts arranged into a whole, to notes arranged into a song, and finally to a mind arranged into calm.
sensesIntro.cn: 从部分排成整体，到音符排成歌曲，最后到心绪排成平静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand placing each part in its place until a whole appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把每个部分放到位，直到整体出现。

branches.en: The basic sense is simply parts placed together.
branches.cn: 基本义项就是各部分被放在一起。

branches.en: Writing music is the same act with notes instead of bricks.
branches.cn: 写音乐只是把砖块换成音符的同一个动作。

branches.en: Calming the mind is composing its scattered pieces.
branches.cn: 让心平静，就是把散乱的碎片重新组合。

branches.en: Both senses depend on choosing an order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都取决于选好一种顺序。

branches.en: A finished song and a calm face both show ordered parts.
branches.cn: 完成的歌曲与平静的面容都显出有序的部分。

intro.en: Compose is built on Latin com-, together, plus ponere, to put, through the French form composer.
intro.cn: compose 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）构成，经法语 composer 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base pos- or pon- also appears in position, deposit and component.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 pos- 或 pon- 也出现在 position、deposit 与 component 中。

items.example: A thin layer composes the outer shell.
items.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的物质构成外壳。

items.example: The panel is composed of six experts.
items.exampleCN: 这个小组由六位专家组成。

items.example: He is composing a new suite.
items.exampleCN: 他正在创作一组新组曲。
这位作曲家住在维也纳。

items.example: The composition of the team changed.

items.exampleCN: 他们用了一张合成照片。

items.example: Leaves decompose slowly in cold weather.

definition_zh: 咨询公司；顾问业；咨询工作
definition_en: a company that gives expert advice, or the business of giving such advice
core_image: 一间玻璃会议室，几个人围着图表向客户讲解
scene: 她毕业两年后进了一家专门提供管理建议的公司。 She works for a small consultancy in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 consultancy 指「咨询公司」（第 1 个义项：提供专业建议的机构）；句意是她在城里一家小型咨询公司工作。

pos.zh: 咨询公司；顾问业；咨询工作

senses.title: A firm of advisers
senses.definition: a company whose business is giving expert advice to clients
senses.definitionCN: 以向客户提供专业建议为业的公司
senses.example: She joined a consultancy after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 她毕业后进了一家咨询公司。
senses.why: Knowledge becomes a product when a firm agrees to sell it.
senses.whyCN: 当一家公司答应出售知识时，知识就成了产品。

senses.title: The advising trade
senses.definition: the work or industry of giving professional advice
senses.definitionCN: 提供专业意见的行当或工作
senses.example: He spent ten years in consultancy before teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 他在咨询行业干了十年才去教书。
senses.why: An entire trade can grow from one repeated question.
senses.whyCN: 一个反复出现的问题，能长成一整个行业。

intro.en: Consultancy is consult plus -ancy, from Latin consultare, to take counsel, a frequent form of consulere.
intro.cn: consultancy 是 consult 加 -ancy，源自拉丁语 consultare（反复商议），是 consulere 的反复形式。

items.en: Consulere meant to gather people for counsel.
items.cn: consulere 意为召集众人商议。

items.en: Consultare repeated the act of asking for advice.
items.cn: consultare 表示反复求取意见。

items.en: The suffix -antia named a state or an activity.
items.cn: 词尾 -antia 表示一种状态或活动。

items.en: English consultant first named a person asked for advice.
items.cn: 英语 consultant 最初指被请教的人。

items.en: Consultancy grew into the name of the advising business itself.
items.cn: consultancy 逐渐成为咨询业本身的名称。

items.en: It now means both a firm and the trade it works in.
items.cn: 如今它既指一家公司，也指这门行业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the consult- family or a similar ending, and the meaning group names other bodies that sell expert service.
note.cn: 形近组共享 consult- 词族或相似词尾，近义组列出其他出售专业服务的机构。

entries.definition: a person who gives expert advice
a meeting held to seek advice
the office of an official who helps citizens abroad
a business that provides a service for others
an official body that gives advice
a professional business, such as a law firm

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a client's problem carried into a glass room, then move to advice sold as a service and to an industry built on trust.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被带进玻璃会议室的客户难题开始，再到被当作服务出售的意见，最后到建立在信任上的行业。

normal.en: Consult plus -ancy means the state of always being asked.
normal.cn: consult 加 -ancy，表示总被人来问的这种状态。

normal.en: A consultancy sells nothing you can hold, only what it knows.
normal.cn: 咨询公司不卖能拿在手里的东西，只卖它知道的东西。

normal.en: The same question asked by many firms becomes an industry.
normal.cn: 许多公司问同一个问题，就长成一个行业。

normal.en: A consultancy lives on its next good answer.
normal.cn: 咨询公司靠下一个好答案活着。

normal.en: They rent out the advice they once gave for free.
normal.cn: 它们把从前免费给的建议租出去。

abstract.en: Picture a glass room with charts on every wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一间四面墙都贴着图表的玻璃会议室。

abstract.en: Picture a folder passed across a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹沿长桌递过去。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate that says adviser, not seller.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写着顾问而非卖家的名牌。

examples.en: The consultancy advised the city on transport planning.
examples.cn: 这家咨询公司为城市的交通规划提供建议。

examples.en: She left banking to start her own consultancy.
examples.cn: 她离开银行业，创办了自己的咨询公司。

examples.en: Consultancy work often means long hours and travel.
examples.cn: 咨询工作常常意味着长时间加班和出差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consultancy 记成 consult（咨询）加 ancy（行业、机构）：专门靠回答别人问题过日子的机构，就是咨询公司。

root: 由 consult（商议、请教）加名词词尾 -ancy 构成，词根为拉丁语 consulere（聚集商议），后指咨询公司与顾问业。

sensesIntro.en: From one firm that answers questions for money, to the whole trade of selling answers.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一家靠回答问题收钱的公司，到整个出售答案的行当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass room where charts are explained to a client.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间玻璃会议室里，有人向客户讲解图表。

branches.en: The first sense is the firm as a place and a name.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是作为场所与名号的公司。

branches.en: The second sense is the trade that all such firms share.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是所有这类公司共有的行当。

branches.en: Every firm is one small piece of the larger trade.
branches.cn: 每家公司都是这更大行业的一小块。

branches.en: Clients return when the advice proves true twice.
branches.cn: 建议两次被证明有效，客户就会回来。

branches.en: The industry grows wherever decisions are too complex for one head.
branches.cn: 哪里的事复杂到一个脑袋装不下，这个行业就在哪里生长。

intro.en: Consultancy is consult plus the noun ending -ancy, meaning a state or a business.
intro.cn: consultancy 是 consult 加名词词尾 -ancy，表示状态或行业。

latinIntro.en: The Latin counsel base consult- also appears in consultant, consultation and consultative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的商议词基 consult- 也出现在 consultant、consultation 与 consultative 中。

items.meaning: a firm or trade that gives advice
items.meaningCN: 提供意见的公司或行业
items.example: The consultancy has offices in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这家咨询公司在三座城市设有办公室。
他们先咨询了一位工程师。

items.meaning: one who is asked for expert advice
items.example: The consultant wrote a short report.
items.exampleCN: 顾问写了一份简短报告。

items.meaning: the act of seeking advice together
items.example: A public consultation begins next week.

items.meaning: having the role of giving advice
items.exampleCN: 这个机构纯粹是咨询性质的。

items.meaning: an official who aids citizens abroad
items.meaningCN: 在海外协助本国公民的官员
items.example: The consul issued a new passport.
items.exampleCN: 领事签发了一本新护照。

items.meaning: careful advice on a serious matter
items.meaningCN: 就严肃问题给出的慎重建议

items.meaning: a rude act that jumps at someone
items.example: The remark was taken as an insult.

definition_zh: 无助的；无能的；没用的
definition_en: not able to help yourself or to change a bad situation
core_image: 手伸出去却抓不到任何东西
scene: 婴儿还太小，完全无助。 The baby is too young and completely helpless.
sceneCN: 这里 helpless 是「无助的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婴儿还太小，完全无助。

senses.title: Without help
senses.definition: unable to take care of yourself
senses.definitionCN: 无法照顾自己的
senses.example: The baby is too young and completely helpless.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿还太小，完全无助。
senses.why: This is the sense of needing another person.
senses.whyCN: 这是需要他人的义项。

senses.title: Powerless
senses.definition: unable to change or stop something
senses.definitionCN: 无法改变或阻止某事
senses.example: We felt helpless against the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 面对暴风雨，我们感到无能为力。
senses.why: The same lack of means applies to a situation.
senses.whyCN: 同样的无力感也用于面对某种处境。

intro.en: Helpless adds the suffix -less to the old verb help.
intro.cn: helpless 由古老的动词 help 加后缀 -less 构成。

items.en: Help came from a root meaning aid.
items.cn: help 源自意为援助的词根。

items.en: Helpan meant to give aid.
items.cn: helpan 意为给予帮助。

items.en: The suffix -less meant without.
items.cn: 后缀 -less 意为没有。

items.en: Helpless described people without aid.
items.cn: helpless 形容得不到帮助的人。

items.en: Helpless widened to mean powerless.
items.cn: helpless 扩展为表示无能为力的。

note.en: Helpless is compared with look-alike words and with words for weakness.
note.cn: 把 helpless 与形近词以及表示无力的词作比较。

entries.definition: unlucky
without hope
thinking of others first
without the ability to act
easy to attack
not strong

normalIntro.en: Helpless means help has been taken away, leaving no way to act.
normalIntro.cn: helpless 意为帮助被拿走，剩下无计可施。

normal.en: The baby is too young and completely helpless.
normal.cn: 婴儿还太小，完全无助。

normal.en: We felt helpless against the storm.
normal.cn: 面对暴风雨，我们感到无能为力。

normal.en: She was helpless with laughter.
normal.cn: 她笑得不能自已。

normal.en: The injured bird lay helpless on the grass.
normal.cn: 受伤的鸟无助地躺在草地上。

normal.en: He felt helpless watching the fire.
normal.cn: 看着大火，他感到无能为力。

abstract.en: Helpless is the moment before someone else's hand arrives.
abstract.cn: 无助，是别人的手伸来之前的那一刻。

abstract.en: To admit helplessness is the first honest strength.
abstract.cn: 承认无助，是第一种诚实的力量。

abstract.en: No one is helpless while they can still ask.
abstract.cn: 只要还能开口求助，就没有人是无助的。

examples.en: The baby is too young and completely helpless.
examples.cn: 婴儿还太小，完全无助。
